office_does: The prosecuting attorney prosecutes crimes in Grays Harbor County on behalf of the state and is the county's civil legal counsel.
race_blurb: Interim Prosecutor Jason Walker (D), appointed by the commissioners effective March 17, 2026, faces his own chief criminal deputy, Daniel Crawford (R), after leading the primary by 38 votes. Both promise to hold offenders accountable and support victims, and the race centers on turnover and stability in the office.

candidates.summary: Chief criminal deputy prosecutor and Marine Corps veteran with more than 100 jury trials, running on aggressive prosecution and accountability.
highlights: Will 'aggressively pursue' violent offenders, child predators, drug traffickers and domestic abusers [S2]
Says repeat offenders are 'too often released only to offend again' [S2]
Wants the worst offenders out and therapeutic courts for 'the people we can help' [S8]
Argued in 2025 for raises for three prosecutors and for filling vacant positions [S7][S8]

experience.basis: Career prosecutor and the office's current chief criminal deputy who has never held elected office and runs as the challenger; insider and outsider elements balance.

safety.basis: Repeated enforcement framing (aggressive prosecution, repeat offenders, pushing more trials) with therapeutic courts reserved for those who can be helped.

spending.basis: Asked the commissioners for about $89,376 a year in raises and said three more prosecutors were needed.

candidates.summary: Interim prosecutor since March 2026, formerly the office's chief criminal deputy and a statewide prosecutor trainer, running on restoring stability to the office.
highlights: Says turnover rose sharply while he was away and that provable charges were reduced or dismissed [S1]
Will prioritize repeat, violent and sex offenders [S4]
Calls himself an early champion of diversion and therapeutic courts, with 'real consequences for failure' [S4]
Opposed proposed court rules capping misdemeanor bail in a 2026 letter to the Supreme Court [S9]

experience.basis: Appointed incumbent with 11 years in the office and four at the statewide prosecutors' association, running on 'proven experience'; no prior elected office.

safety.basis: Prioritizes repeat and violent offenders and opposed looser misdemeanor bail, while explicitly championing diversion and therapeutic courts.
